description: An eight-step sequencer with one voltage per step and a gate on every step, running from its own tempo or from a clock you patch in

params.text: Sets the voltage this step sends, 0V at the bottom of its travel and 10V at the top
Sets the tempo from 40 to 200 beats per minute while no clock is patched, and picks the multiplier a quarter, a half, one, two or four times the clock once one is

inputs.text: Steps the sequence on each pulse, and turns the tempo control into a multiplier while it has a cable
Returns the sequence to step one on a trigger, and wins over a clock pulse arriving on the same sample

outputs.text: The voltage of the step the sequence is on, 0V to 10V
A one millisecond pulse at 10V on every step, including steps whose voltage is zero

notes: the sequence runs on its own tempo as soon as the module is placed; there is no start control and no way to stop it short of bypassing the module
the lamp beside the tempo control pulses at the rate the sequence is running and brightens as that rate rises
changing the multiplier while a clock is patched restarts the internal phase count, so the sequence does not drift away from the clock
